[Rating: 3/10] Is it total luck?  Is there skill?  I don't really care.  Its just not that interesting even with the scoring gimmicks.  I won the game and several times literally shuffled my hand and played a random card.

[Rating: 3/10] A few too many "yes, but!" twists stacked on top of regular ol' trick-taking. As a player I felt too far removed from the final scoring (which of course also had a twist) to enjoy myself.  edit after 2nd play: What a mess of a design. Feels like it subverts expectations at every turn for the sake of it, with little regard for cohesion. Very chaotic. Tension was low until players accumulate enough points to be near the game-ending 40. Almost nothing clicked for me with this one.

[Rating: 3/10] I just don't see the appeal. At least one player in our group holds this in high regard, but I don't see having that much control in this game, so a massive con there. Tried at 3-5p, I liked 4p the best, then 5p, I wouldn't play with 3p. I just feel that there isn't much play to be had here.

[Rating: 5/10] I like this KIND of game, but I didn't understand a damn thing that happened when I played, and it seems like constantly re-checking what a given play would do to each person's score is no fun. So I played on intuition and felt baffled. Is there a middle road?

[Rating: 5/10] First impression: Willing to play this more, but I had a few issues:  1. The game doesn’t really feel “afoot” until someone gets close to going over. Meaning the first couple rounds feel like you’re going through the motions.  2. There are a lot of tools, but most of them are used to hurt other people — not help yourself. I think having a lot of a certain color is the lever to pull. But overall you feel a little too out of control.  3. Referring to number 1, the last round is the only one that matters.
